title: POC Weekly: Deployment Blockers & KMS Handoff
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on resolving two deployment blockers: KMS/HSM integration for key management and a network egress policy that prevented staging calls. Discussed fallbacks (hosted vs dedicated), bench results showing 18% higher tail latency with current config, and plan to exchange security docs. Agreed next steps include KMS playbook, run targeted latency bench (quantized model), and schedule cross-team runbook review.
next_steps: Redwood: Share KMS integration guide and sample IAM policy by 2026-02-02
Kestrel: Provision a test KMS key and share ARN with Redwood by 2026-02-03
Redwood SE: Run 2 targeted latency benches with q4 quantized build and share CSV results by 2026-02-05
action_items: Ava Martinez: Send KMS integration playbook + sample Terraform (due: 2026-02-02)
Ravi Shah: Kick off quantized latency bench and upload raw results to drive (due: 2026-02-05)
Ethan Cole: Create test KMS key and provide ARN + staging network allowlist (due: 2026-02-03)
Priya Nair: Share SOC2 scoping questions and list of compliance docs needed (due: 2026-02-04)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-29
Time: 15:30 UTC (scheduled 45m)
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Ravi Shah (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Marta Liu (Kestrel), Ethan Cole (Kestrel), Priya Nair (Kestrel), Andre Gomez (Kestrel)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — say hi and roles so we have the right folks on the record.
[00:06] Marta: Hi this is Marta, head of MLOps at Kestrel.
[00:10] Ethan: Ethan, platform eng — I'm the infra owner for the staging cluster.
[00:13] Priya: Priya, security.
[00:15] Andre: Andre, CTO — will hop in for the last 10.
[00:18] Ava: Great, from Redwood we have Ravi and Lena as well. We're here to unblock the two items you flagged: KMS/HSM integration and that staging egress rule that blocked calls last week.
[00:28] Marta: Yeah, those two are the big ones. Also imp to discuss the latency numbers you sent — the tail was higher than we expected on the 8k sequence runs.

[02:00] Ravi: Quick context — the bench you saw was run on our q4 quantized runtime (experimental kernels). We saw median token latency good, but 95/99 tail spikes when the prefix was long and batch dynamics changed. Could be KV cache miss pattern or garbage collection on the instance.
[02:22] Ethan: Do you have logs that tie tail spikes to certain host events? We saw some preemption activity in GCP that correlates but not sure it's causal.
[02:34] Ravi: We captured traces — I'll share a trace bundle. There's some noise around KV eviction when multiple requests hit and we warmed up with discontinuous prefixes. Might be mitigated with sticky-hot partitioning or larger KV cache.

[05:10] Priya: From security — KMS is a blocker. We can't ship keys to anyone. We need either customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) with HSM-backed keys or an approved (air-gapped) HSM path for private deployments. What options does Redwood offer?
[05:26] Ava: Good — we support both patterns. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in the customer's cloud KMS via a federated key-ARN approach. For Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS over a secured link; for Private on-prem we can plug into an HSM. There are some config differences per mode.
[05:46] Marta: Can you share concrete IAM policy snippets and a terraform example? Our security team needs to validate before provisioning.
[05:52] Ava: Yes — action: I'll send a KMS integration playbook + sample Terraform snippets.

[07:30] Ethan: The other blocker was egress — the staging environment didn't allow outbound to the Redwood gateway so the agent couldn't reach the inference endpoint. We opened a ticket but need a minimal allowlist. What's the minimal set of FQDNs/IP ranges and ports?
[07:45] Lena: We can provide a short allowlist: gateway.redwood.ai, metrics.redwood.ai, and the region-specific inference pool IP ranges. We'll put that into the playbook too.
[07:58] Ethan: Perfect, that should let us test without broad egress.

[10:05] Ravi: Back to performance — two immediate knobs: increase KV cache to reduce evictions, and a batching policy tweak that reduces dynamic batch churn. Neither requires code changes, just service config. We can test both in staging once egress/KMS are sorted.
[10:24] Marta: On the dedicated vs hosted question — if we go hosted for the pilot it's faster to get live but we need to ensure PHI is never stored unencrypted and we keep control of keys. Priya: thoughts?
[10:36] Priya: Hosted is okay if we control KMS keys and can get audit evidence. We'll need SOC2 evidence, access logs, and retention policy. Without that we prefer dedicated in our VPC.

[12:00] Ava: For SOC2 and logging we have a compliance packet and can provide audit log exports for the session-level events. We'll attach the packet to the notes.
[12:12] Andre: Quick question — what's the fallback if performance suffers on hosted? Can Redwood route to a cheaper variant or fallback to a quantized model?
[12:24] Ravi: Yes, smart routing can fallback by policy to a quantized variant or to a different region. For the pilot we can pin a canary that uses q4 quantized and another that uses full-fp16; routing policy will prefer the minimal-latency profile. There is a small quality delta with quantized models which we can measure with your eval set.

[15:05] Ethan: About the latency bench you mentioned — what's the exact harness so we can reproduce? We need the request distribution, sequence lengths, and concurrency settings.
[15:15] Ravi: I'll share the bench harness — it's a JMeter+python wrapper that replays saved prompts with a user mix. We used 70% short <128 token, 20% mid 1k-2k, and 10% long 8k sequences; concurrency was 24 and the batcher dynamic target was 128 tokens.
[15:35] Marta: Can you run one bench with sticky-hot partitioning and one without, so we can quantify delta?
[15:41] Ravi: Yes — I'll run two targeted benches and upload CSVs.

[18:10] Priya: On KMS specifics: we need proof of key isolation, rotation support, and HSM-backed SRK. Also logs for key usage. Is Redwood able to surface KMS audit logs in the console or export them?
[18:25] Ava: We can export key usage events to your monitoring via a secure push — or you can pull them from your KMS. For Dedicated and Private we can integrate with your SIEM. We'll include a diagram in the playbook.

[20:00] Marta: Also timeline — we aimed to be in limited pilot by mid-February, downstream product launch in late Q2. Is the Kestrel timeline doable with these blockers?
[20:09] Ava: If we move quickly on KMS provisioning and allowlist and Redwood runs the two benches, mid-February for a limited pilot is realistic. The critical path is your KMS key and the staging egress.

[22:50] Ethan: One nit — earlier you mentioned 'KV cache' behavior causing spikes. If we increase the cache, how does that impact memory footprint and cost? We have constrained instance families in staging.
[23:05] Ravi: Increasing KV cache will increase RAM usage per shard; on GPUs that translates to slightly fewer replicas per host. We'll estimate unit economics and include a recommended memory / replica sizing table. If cost is a concern we can try sticky partitioning first which usually reduces tail without doubling RAM.

[25:00] Priya: For the compliance packet — can we get redacted SOC2 artifacts or a statement of control? Legal needs something to review.
[25:10] Lena: Yes, we can provide a SOC2 summary and a standard SOC2 letter; for full artifacts we can start an NDA process — but we typically provide a SOC2 report under CDA.

[28:20] Marta: Would Redwood allow us to run an on-prem demo in an air-gapped environment later? We may need that for PHI workloads.
[28:28] Ava: Absolutely — Private on-prem is an option. It requires additional integration (HSM, local monitoring) and a longer lead time but it's on the roadmap for regulated workloads. We'll scope that separately.

[31:00] Ravi: Quick note — there's also a config flag to lower priority background GC during high concurrency; that helped another customer reduce 99th percentile by ~12%. I can turn that on in a staging shard for testing.
[31:18] Ethan: Please do that for one bench run. It'll help isolate cause.

[34:05] Andre: Sorry I'm late. I've skimmed notes — key question: what's failure mode if the KMS talk fails mid-request? We can't have plaintext in logs or temp disk.
[34:20] Ravi: Good question. We use envelope encryption — model payloads are encrypted and keys never traverse in plaintext. If KMS fails we have a fallback to deny request; we also have grace periods and local ephemeral keys for short windows but those are gated by policy. We'll document failure modes in the playbook.

[36:50] Priya: Also need RBAC — who can decrypt in your console? We need role separation and audit for operators.
[37:02] Ava: We support RBAC mapping to SSO groups (SAML/Okta) and will provide a default role matrix.

[40:00] Ava: Let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[40:05] Ava: Action items: Redwood to send KMS playbook + allowlist + SOC2 summary; Redwood SE to run two benches (sticky partition + GC tweak) and share CSVs; Kestrel to create test KMS key and allowlist egress to gateway; Priya to list compliance docs needed.
[40:25] Marta: Sounds good — please include the bench harness and the exact command lines so our infra can reproduce.
[40:30] Ravi: Will do.
[42:10] Lena: I'll schedule the runbook walkthrough for 2026-02-08 10:00 PT and send calendar invites after the call.
[42:18] Andre: I'll join the runbook review.
[42:22] Ava: Great — any final questions?
[42:30] Ethan: None here.
[42:33] Priya: No.
[42:35] Ava: Cool, we'll follow up and close the KMS egress path first. Thanks everyone.
[42:45] Meeting end: 15:15 PT / 23:15 UTC
notes: References: KMS playbook (to be shared) — link placeholder: https://redwood.ai/playbooks/kms-integration (will be attached), bench harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness (private), compliance packet: attached SOC2-summary.pdf
